title: Eisenhower never drew a box in his life.
description:
Eisenhower never drew a box in his life.

Eisenhower quoted a line at the World Council of Churches: 'I have two kinds of problems, the urgent and the important. The urgent are not important, and the important are never urgent.' He credited it to 'a former college president', not to himself, and not by name.

Northwestern's president, who introduced Eisenhower that day and is named earlier in the speech. He is not the 'former college president' Eisenhower actually quotes, though most retellings assume he is.

The gap between Eisenhower's speech and the year the four quadrant grid people picture was actually invented.

Turned Eisenhower's two sentences into the four quadrant grid in his book The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People, more than three decades after the speech.

Sources:
- https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/address-the-second-assembly-the-world-council-churches-evanston-illinois - the full primary transcript, read in full: on 19 August 1954 at Northwestern University, Eisenhower says he is quoting the statement of 'a former college president', without naming him, then quotes the line 'I have two kinds of problems, the urgent and the important. The urgent are not important, and the important are never urgent.' The published footnote separately identifies Dr J. Roscoe Miller as the Northwestern president who introduced Eisenhower that day, a different role from the unnamed college president the quote is actually credited to.
- https://www.todoist.com/productivity-methods/eisenhower-matrix - read in full: confirms that more than three decades after the 1954 speech, Stephen Covey's 1989 book The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People repackaged the quote into the four quadrant grid now called the Eisenhower Matrix.
